source: Written for this app, from the harmlessness rules in a user-supplied pet-comedy series brief ('harmless slapstick: soft feline paw swats without extended claws. Zero genuine pain, hostility, or fear' / 'no dangerous heights, sharp objects, toxic substances, or choking hazards'). NOT transcribed from the AI Video Bootcamp course, and not measured from reference video.
note: The app's first CONTENT gate. Every other linter in this project judges how an image is MADE - realism layers, structural completeness, continuity. This one judges what it DEPICTS. Two rules make it safe to run: (1) it scans only human-authored fields, never an assembled prompt and never a sound brief, because the shared vocabulary is full of innocent collisions - 'crushing' lives in camera_angle_bank, 'squash and stretch' in story_bank's stylised style, 'slap' and 'smacked' in sound_bank's comedy examples; (2) it is opt-in per format, listed only in `sitcom`'s checks, so `story` and `trade` are provably unaffected - trade's own shipped mishap 'one shoves the other and it lands flat on its back' would fail the softener rule, and widening a gate to content written before it turns a correct linter into a nuisance.
matching_note: Each category carries TWO lists, and the split is not cosmetic. `stems` are start-anchored, so 'claw' catches 'claws' and 'clawing'; `words` are whole-word, so 'pain' does not fire on 'a painted wall'. Start-anchoring everything breaks on 'pain'; whole-wording everything misses 'swatting'. This is the same plain-word-versus-phrase distinction realism_lint._layer_key_present already draws, for the same reason. Negation is NOT re-implemented here: safety_lint imports realism_lint.is_negated, so 'no claws' reads as safe everywhere the shared gate would read it that way.

defused.note: is_negated() is a PREFIX rule - it looks backwards from the term. A phrase that defuses itself AFTER the word escapes it entirely, so these are stripped from the text before anything is scanned. Measured: 'claws sheathed' reads as a positive claw hit without this.

injury.label: No injury
injury.role: Nothing may be described as damaging the animal.
injury.fix: Say what the animal does, not what it costs. A tap is an event; a scratch is an injury.

distress.label: No genuine distress
distress.role: The comedy is performed outrage, never real fear.
distress.fix: A cat throwing a theatrical tantrum is funny. A frightened cat is not. Describe the performance, not the feeling.

hazard.label: No dangerous set
hazard.role: Nothing sharp, hot, toxic, electrical or high may be staged near the animal.
hazard.fix: Swap the prop. The brief's own rule is safe miniatures - a rubber phone, a plush burger, a soft silicone bottle.

softened.label: Contact is softened
softened.role: A contact word is fine - unsoftened contact is not.
softened.note: The one POSITIVE rule here: the others fail on what is present, this one fails on what is MISSING. It passes trivially when no contact word appears at all, the same way story_lint.check_tasks_vary passes when there is nothing to compare. Scoped per field, not across the joined text, so a 'soft daylight' in the setting cannot vouch for a swat in the action.
softened.fix: Name the softness in the same breath as the contact: 'a soft cartoon-like paw tap, claws in' rather than 'a swat'.
softened.stem_note: Both forms are listed where an inflection drops the stem's final letter. 'shoving' does not contain 'shove', and the shorter stem that would catch it - 'shov' - also catches 'shovelling wet cement', which story_bank ships as a construction task. Explicit forms beat a stem that catches a shovel.

audit_allow.note: Reviewed collisions. safety_lint --check-bank fails on any collision NOT listed here, so a term added later that fires on shipped vocabulary is caught the day it lands. Each entry says why the collision is acceptable: in every case the phrase lives in vocabulary that cannot reach a human-authored scene field - a sound-effect prompt, a colour-grade reference, a style example, a camera-angle description.

allow.why: An ElevenLabs sound-effect prompt from the course's own 100. Sound briefs are never scanned - rule 1 in safety_lint's docstring - and 'punch' must stay a harm word.
The film, not the object. A colour-grade reference; 'blade' stays a hazard word.
A camera-movement example describing a battlefield shot. Motion examples are not scene fields.
Two style examples set on rooftops. A rooftop genuinely is a hazard for a cat, so the term stays; these are style vocabulary, not staging.
A low-angle description of how a SUBJECT reads to the viewer, not a distressed animal.
